scope: TradingView preconditions for the build-3 source: automated transfer onto the operator-renamed saved document, automated 13-input BUS rebinding, layout persistence, operator alert swap, and alert readback; not replay-case evidence (see the build-3 replay artifact of the same date)

source.hashScheme: sha256 over freeze_library_pin(source) -- refresh-invariant, identical to the contract buildHistory scheme

transfer.mechanism: declarationTitle-aware batch save (#4736) onto the saved document the operator renamed to 'SMC Hold Manager' (#4753 aligned declaration and payload wire label): buffer asserted to declare 'SMC Hold Manager', staged and post-save source hash-verified against the repository
transfer.note: An earlier targeted save (run 31945810554, 2026-08-16T11:59Z) verified the same staged and post-save source but was dispatched without force_rebind; the save reset the chart instance's 13 input.source selections to defaults and the run went red on its own binding verify. The run named above re-saved every rollout surface WITH force_rebind and is the authoritative transfer: any source save resets input.source bindings, so a write dispatch is never issued without force_rebind.

tradingView.bindingReverification: tv-save-consumer-source 31948499911 (2026-08-16T12:59Z, verify-only, after the operator's alert swap): 13/13 selections matching, outOfBandDrift clean
tradingView.bindingBaselinePublished: bot/live-tradingview-bindings 30a816c76 (2026-08-16T13:02:41Z) covers the Hold Manager with 13 matching selections

alertReadback.summary: one build-pinned alert Active on BKNG 5m after the operator deleted the build-2 alert and created one on the build-3 instance; zero legacy channel alerts remaining

limitations: The transfer and binding evidence are CI-run reports (uploaded artifacts of the runs named above), not an interactive re-measurement in this artifact.
The alert's webhook action being enabled is not machine-verified (the per-alert edit dialog stays closed); delivery is proven by the receiver's state endpoint once the first live edge fires.

The new alert row is name-identical to the build-2 row it replaced (TradingView derives the default name from the instance legend). That it snapshots the build-3 instance rests on the operator's delete-and-recreate in this sitting; the receiver's sourceBuild validation on first delivery is the machine check.
